probes.query: A span arrives that has no start time recorded. For each of the four storage implementations (in-memory, Elasticsearch, Cassandra, MySQL), how does the write path treat time for that span, and can a time-bounded search find it afterwards?
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: Elasticsearch writes the span into the index of its first annotation's time (else the current time), but BulkIndexWriter.addSearchFields writes no timestamp_millis when the span timestamp is zero, so time-ranged searches cannot match it.
CRITICAL: Cassandra uses guessTimestamp (first annotation with timestamp > 0, else 0); when the guess is 0, accept skips the trace_by_service_span and remote-service index rows.
Cassandra still writes the span row (ts_uuid falls back to the current time) and the service/span-name row before that skip.
MySQL sets start_ts only when the timestamp is non-zero and has no fallback, so a start_ts BETWEEN search never returns it.
In-memory keys the span at timestamp 0, which sorts as the oldest trace (evicted first) and falls outside lowTraceIdsInRange.

probes.query: On Cassandra, traces older than a short while still open when requested by ID but never show up in search results, even when the search window is set very long. Which code and schema settings cause this?
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: CassandraSpanStore.timestampRange clamps the start of the search window to max(endTs - lookback, now - indexTtl).

probes.query: A message arrives on the Kafka topic. Under which conditions is it ignored, counted as dropped, decoded as a single legacy span, or handed to the general list decoder, and what happens in the list decoder when the first byte is unrecognised?
expectedFacts: Every record increments the message and byte counters first; an empty value is then ignored with no further counting.
A value shorter than 2 bytes increments the dropped-messages counter and is skipped.

CRITICAL: A value that is not protobuf3 (first byte 10 with a non-zero second byte), whose first byte is <= 16 and not 12, is decoded as a single span with THRIFT.decodeOne; a RuntimeException there counts a dropped message.

Every other value (protobuf3, a thrift list starting with 12, JSON starting with '[', or any other byte) goes to collector.acceptSpans(bytes, NOOP), which uses SpanBytesDecoderDetector.decoderForListMessage.
CRITICAL: decoderForListMessage accepts first bytes 12, 11, protobuf3 or '[' and otherwise throws IllegalArgumentException, which Collector.handleDecodeError counts as a dropped message.

probes.query: When the server is set up to trace its own work, what decides whether a given incoming request starts a trace of the server itself? Cover how the percentage setting and the per-second cap setting interact, and which requests are even considered.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: When the percentage is not 1.0 the sampler is BoundarySampler below 0.01 and Sampler.create(rate) otherwise, and the per-second cap is ignored.
When the percentage is 1.0 and the per-second cap is non-zero, RateLimitingSampler.create(cap) is used (the defaults 1.0 and 1 give one trace per second).
When the percentage is 1.0 and the cap is 0, Sampler.ALWAYS_SAMPLE is used.

CRITICAL: The Tracing itself uses Sampler.NEVER_SAMPLE; only HttpTracing's serverSampler can start traces, and it consults the sampler only for paths starting with /api or /zipkin/api (other paths return false).
Consequently traces cannot start from other sources such as Kafka or RabbitMQ consumers (sampler javadoc).

probes.query: When the server traces its own work and Cassandra is the storage backend, where does each individual database statement execution become a child span of the request's trace?
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: It does not: ZipkinCassandra3StorageConfiguration imports TracingSessionFactoryEnhancer (@ConditionalOnSelfTracing) but its postProcessAfterInitialization returns the bean unchanged; the TracingSession wrapping is commented out.
The zipkin-storage-cassandra module contains no Brave code and DefaultSessionFactory builds untraced sessions.
The Cassandra driver instrumentation dependency is commented out in zipkin-server/pom.xml.
